The project is a FastAPI login API whose services in app/services/ use only the Python standard library; their pytest tests in tests/unit/ pass. app/services/auth.py has authenticate_user(email, password, *, client_ip, users, store), which returns the user or None; client_ip is used only in a log line, and store, a CounterStore that the router passes in, is not used yet. app/services/counter_store.py defines the CounterStore protocol (get, incr, expire, ttl, delete), CounterStoreError, which every store method raises when the store fails, InMemoryCounterStore, which takes a clock, and RedisCounterStore for production. The router in app/routers/auth.py returns the same 401 for an unknown email and a wrong password. The scope has AC-001: after 5 failed login attempts for an email address within 15 minutes, further attempts for that address are refused for 15 minutes with 429 and Retry-After; and AC-002: login does not reveal whether an account exists. The scope leaves to the design whether a successful login resets an address's failed attempts, and its non-goals include changes to password hashing and to login response timing. The technical design adds AccountLockedError(retry_after) to app/services/auth.py, raised by authenticate_user while an email address is locked; counts failed attempts in the CounterStore that authenticate_user receives; adds the settings login_lockout_threshold = 5 and login_lockout_seconds = 900 to app/config.py, which the router passes to authenticate_user as two new keyword-only parameters, lockout_threshold and lockout_seconds, that default to the same 5 and 900, so app/services/ still imports only the standard library and app/services/; lets a CounterStoreError from the store propagate out of authenticate_user, so no login succeeds while the store fails, and has the router answer it with 503 and the detail "Login is temporarily unavailable"; and has the router map AccountLockedError to 429 with a Retry-After header. It leaves how failed attempts are counted in the store, including whether a successful login resets them, to the developer as an implementation detail.
